newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indosat, Kazakh firm in joint venture.
newsitem.headline: Indosat, Kazakh firm in joint venture.

text.p: Indonesia's PT Indonesia Satellite Corp (Indosat) said on Thursday it had signed an agreement with a Kazakh firm and another Indonesian company to jointly provide telecommunication services in Kazakhstan.

Indosat said they have agreed to establish a limited liability company, Inkatel, which will provide telecommunication services for local, long distance and international calls, with the first major customers expected to come from the central Asian republic's oil and gas industry.

Indosat said the Limited Liability Partnership Jarykh of Kazakhstan will own a 50-percent stake in the venture, while Indosat holds 40 percent and the rest to be held by Indonesian firm PT Prima Comexindo.
Indosat said the budgetted capital expenditure of Inkatel was $4.2 million until 1998, while its paid-up capital would be $4.75 million.
Indonesia's state-controlled Indosat is listed on the New York and Jakarta stock exchanges.
